target_reviews.assessment_reason: Direct cause: no scientific mismatch was found for the nine paper-exact n=100 profiles. Root cause of residual finite-size differences from the red cosine guide is the guide's asymptotic status, not a model mismatch. Code-fault assessment: no defect found after dense-Liouvillian and reflection/bounds checks; the isolated rerun reproduced the frozen hashes.

independent_checks.claim: Transfer profiles agree with a dense Liouvillian fixed point at small n.
Profiles obey reflection antisymmetry and Pauli-z bounds.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: Main Fig. 2(a) profiles follow the paper's exact transfer construction at the printed parameters.
falsification_attempts.method: Compare all curves against symmetry bounds, dense fixed points, and the isotropic continuum limit.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: Direct cause: no mismatch remains in the main current panel over n=2..400. Root cause of the three curve families is the easy-plane, isotropic, and easy-axis transfer spectra described by the paper. Code-fault assessment: no defect found; dense currents, bond conservation, n^-2 coefficient, and deterministic rerun all pass.

independent_checks.claim: Transfer currents match a direct dense Liouvillian solver and are bond independent.
The isotropic current approaches pi^2/(epsilon n^2) through n=400.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: Main Fig. 2(b) current curves and isotropic guide are scientifically correct.
falsification_attempts.method: Check dense small-n values, local conservation, full plotted size domain, and asymptotic exponent/coefficient.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: Direct cause: every easy-axis fit has the printed slope within 1.8e-13 and R^2 above 0.9999985. Root cause is the hyperbolic transfer spectrum. Code-fault assessment: no defect found after dense-current comparison and an independent log-linear fit.

independent_checks.claim: The printed exponent equals -arcosh(3/2).
All three couplings recover the same exponent on n=30..100.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The Fig. 2(b) inset shows coupling-independent exponential rate exp[-n arcosh(3/2)].
falsification_attempts.method: Fit each coupling separately and test semilog linearity.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: Direct cause: the closed Delta=1/2 current agrees with the leading-eigenvalue result and finite n=400 values. Root cause of the nonmonotonic curve is the exact 3x3 transfer spectrum. Code-fault assessment: no defect found; small- and large-epsilon limits plus the maximum were independently checked.

independent_checks.claim: The leading eigenvalue of the printed 3x3 matrix yields the stated J_infinity.
J/epsilon tends to 1/2, epsilon J tends to 4/3, and the maximum is near 1.63.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The Delta=1/2 thermodynamic current formula and its three limiting claims are correct.
falsification_attempts.method: Diagonalize the reduced matrix and probe both coupling extremes and the maximum.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: Direct cause: the printed leading kernel assigns different O(1/n) coefficients to reflection-plus-spin-flip-related point pairs, with minimum scaled gap 0.00856579, while finite exact NESS values agree across the pairs within 7.12e-14. Root cause: a variable/sign transcription error in the printed f(x,y) is strongly indicated. Code-fault assessment: no reproduction-code defect found; transfer correlations match direct density traces to 1.06e-15 and an independent symmetry derivation reaches the same contradiction.

independent_checks.claim: Reflection plus global spin flip requires C(x,y)=C(1-y,1-x), but the printed kernel violates it.
Transfer correlations agree with direct dense density-matrix traces, and finite mirror pairs agree to numerical precision.
The discrepancy persists for n=40,80,120 while the exact mirror gap stays below 7.12e-14.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The paper's explicit leading connected-correlation kernel is compatible with the exact reflection-plus-spin-flip symmetry.
falsification_attempts.method: Evaluate f(x,y) and f(1-y,1-x) at two mirror-related bulk pairs and compare to exact finite NESS correlations over three sizes.

discrepancy.paper_claim: C(x,y)=pi f(min(x,y),max(x,y))/(4n)+O(n^-2) with the printed explicit f.
discrepancy.independent_result: The exact NESS symmetry forces identical leading coefficients at (x,y) and (1-y,1-x); finite transfer and dense checks obey the symmetry, but the printed f does not.
discrepancy.observed_gap: The printed scaled mirror coefficient differs by at least 0.0085657908, whereas finite mirror-pair differences are at most 7.1166e-14.
discrepancy.uncertainty_or_tolerance_basis: The gap is O(1/n), not the stated O(n^-2) remainder; it exceeds the 1e-10 symmetry tolerance by more than seven orders of magnitude after scaling.

Code-fault assessment: no defect found after two n values, two epsilon values, and dense small-chain comparison.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: A local observable can be evaluated in O(n^2) arithmetic operations.
falsification_attempts.method: Count every diagonal and off-diagonal multiplication on the exact reachable band.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: Direct cause: direct Eq. (7) substitution gives the paper-named a_m^+ (odd m) or a_m^- (even m) nonzero, with magnitude at least 0.382683 for m=3..8; the zero occurs in the opposite component at r=m-1 with residual at most 1.29e-16. Root cause: the prose shifts the cutoff index by one and swaps the parity/component, thereby also misstating dimension m+1 instead of m. Code-fault assessment: no defect found; 80-digit analytic evaluation, the full amplitude arrays, and the paper's own m=3 3x3 Eq. (19) all independently agree on the corrected cutoff.

independent_checks.claim: At lambda=pi/m, direct trigonometric substitution makes the paper-named r=m component proportional to sin(pi/m), not zero, while the opposite r=m-1 component contains sin(pi)=0.
Full amplitude arrays for m=3..8 reproduce the corrected parity/index and the printed m=3 three-state matrix.
The corrected zero is at machine precision for six denominators while the claimed component remains order one.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: For lambda=pi l/m, a_m^+=0 for odd m or a_m^-=0 for even m and the closed auxiliary dimension is m+1.
falsification_attempts.method: Substitute the complete printed Eq. (7) at r=m and r=m-1 for m=3..8 and compare with Eq. (19).

discrepancy.paper_claim: At lambda=pi l/m, a_m^+=0 for odd m or a_m^-=0 for even m, so the transfer process closes on H_{m+1}.
discrepancy.independent_result: For l=1 and m=3..8, the nonzero paper-named component has magnitude 0.382683..0.866025; the exact zero is a^-_{m-1} for odd m or a^+_{m-1} for even m, giving m states and matching the printed m=3 3x3 matrix.
discrepancy.paper_source_ref: paper p.4, root-of-unity paragraph before Eq. (19)
discrepancy.observed_gap: Index m versus m-1, plus/minus parity swapped, and auxiliary dimension m+1 versus m.
discrepancy.uncertainty_or_tolerance_basis: The claimed component is bounded away from zero by 0.382683, while the corrected component residual is <=1.2909e-16; the separation exceeds floating uncertainty by over 15 orders of magnitude.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: Direct cause: every entry of the printed Delta=1/2 3x3 matrix is reproduced within 2.78e-16 for all three couplings. Root cause is the corrected three-state root-of-unity closure. Code-fault assessment: no defect found; the matrix was checked entrywise and independently used for its eigenvalue limit.

independent_checks.claim: Substituting lambda=pi/3 into Eq. (7) yields Eq. (19).
All printed matrix entries match for epsilon=1,1/5,1/25.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: Eq. (19) is the correct three-state Delta=1/2 transfer matrix.
falsification_attempts.method: Construct T from the generic amplitudes and compare entrywise at each coupling.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: Direct cause: easy-axis profiles differ across couplings by at most 1.82e-12 and all current slopes equal -arcosh(3/2). Root cause is the dominant easy-axis transfer eigenstructure. Code-fault assessment: no defect found after independent profile-spread and slope checks.

independent_checks.claim: The kink profile is nearly epsilon independent at all three printed couplings.
The large-n current slope is -arcosh(3/2).

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The easy-axis regime has kink profiles and insulating exponential current decay.
falsification_attempts.method: Compare all printed couplings for profile collapse and independently fit their log-current slopes.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: Direct cause: every printed regularized Delta=1 amplitude agrees exactly through the configured auxiliary dimension. Root cause is the specified tau and c scaling before lambda tends to zero. Code-fault assessment: no defect found after direct limit derivation and recurrence comparison.

independent_checks.claim: The lambda-to-zero limit with the printed regularization yields all seven isotropic amplitudes.
Implemented amplitudes match the printed recurrences at three couplings and ten auxiliary levels.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The regularized isotropic amplitudes are the lambda-to-zero limit of Eq. (7).
falsification_attempts.method: Take the prescribed scaled limit separately for odd and even indices and compare finite-r arrays.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: Direct cause: the double commutator and both boundary identities pass at 8.73e-15 or better, and the normalization sequence extrapolates to alpha=0.0344186. Root cause is the isotropic transfer algebra and a slowly convergent O(1/n) remainder. Code-fault assessment: no scientific defect found; double precision becomes cancellation-sensitive beyond the configured alpha window, but the frozen n<=200 extrapolation is corroborated by independent high-precision continuation and does not alter the reported result.

independent_checks.claim: The double-commutator and boundary relations hold away from the artificial cutoff.
A controlled 1/n sequence and extrapolation recover alpha near 0.0346.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: Eqs. (20)-(22), including alpha approximately 0.0346, follow from the isotropic transfer process.
falsification_attempts.method: Check exact matrix identities at several truncations and extrapolate the normalization ratio over ten sizes.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: Direct cause: finite isotropic profiles converge monotonically to cos(pi x), with RMSE falling from 0.00853 at n=40 to 0.000417 at n=160. Root cause is the continuum equation and boundary conditions. Code-fault assessment: no defect found after analytic ODE solution and four-size convergence.

independent_checks.claim: M''=-pi^2 M with M(0)=-M(1)=1 gives M=cos(pi x).
Finite profile error decreases with exponent about -2.17 over n=40..160.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The isotropic strong-driving continuum profile is cos(pi x).
falsification_attempts.method: Solve the continuum boundary-value problem and compare four independently contracted finite chains.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: Direct cause: fitted finite-current error ratios match |lambda_2/lambda_1| within 1.03e-4 relative and bulk profiles flatten monotonically. Root cause is spectral decomposition of the exact 3x3 transfer matrix. Code-fault assessment: no defect found after eigenvalue and independent finite-contraction checks.

independent_checks.claim: The subleading-to-leading eigenvalue ratio controls exponential finite-size corrections.
Direct finite-current errors and bulk profiles follow the spectral predictions at all three couplings.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: Easy-plane observables converge exponentially at the transfer spectral ratio and the thermodynamic profile is flat.
falsification_attempts.method: Compare eigenspectrum predictions with n=8..36 contractions and Perron-state magnetization.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: Direct cause: nonzero shifted triangular minors exist through rank 12 for Delta=1,1.2,1.5, with analytic witnesses matching to 1.41e-16 relative. Root cause is the nonvanishing upper hopping amplitude at every auxiliary level. Code-fault assessment: no defect found after analytic nonzero-witness derivation and independent finite-minor construction. Scope note: this authored target was absent as a standalone row in the frozen fresh inventory and therefore contributes to incomplete scope reconciliation even though its scientific assessment is supported.

independent_checks.claim: For Delta=1 the relevant real parts are nonzero; for Delta>1 the hyperbolic imaginary parts are nonzero at arbitrary r.
Shifted triangular minors have nonzero predicted diagonals at every tested rank.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The transfer matrix has infinite rank for Delta>=1.
falsification_attempts.method: Construct arbitrarily extendable nonsingular shifted minors and verify finite certificates.

findings.claim: The printed isotropic connected-correlation kernel violates an exact reflection-plus-spin-flip symmetry at leading O(1/n), while two independent numerical constructions respect the symmetry.
reproduction_steps: Read the explicit f(x,y) in the final isotropic paragraph of paper/raw/paper.pdf.
Derive C(j,k)=C(n+1-k,n+1-j) from reflection plus global spin flip of the boundary-driven model.
Evaluate the printed kernel on the mirror pairs represented in generated_data/outputs/data/correlation_checks.csv and multiply the difference by n.

Compare the nonzero printed coefficient gap with the finite transfer correlations, and verify the transfer correlator against direct dense density traces using implementation/src/open_xxz/liouvillian.py.

findings.claim: The root-of-unity prose has an off-by-one cutoff, swapped plus/minus parity, and wrong auxiliary dimension; the corrected cutoff is at r=m-1 in the opposite hopping component and yields m states.
reproduction_steps: Read Eq. (7) and the root-of-unity paragraph before Eq. (19) in paper/raw/paper.pdf.
Substitute lambda=pi/m into the complete odd/even amplitudes at r=m and r=m-1.
For m=3..8, compare the claimed component magnitudes and corrected zero residuals in generated_data/outputs/data/quantitative_claims.json.
Check the independent internal consistency condition that the paper's own m=3 example is a 3x3, not 4x4, transfer matrix.

findings.claim: The authored scope is not atomic: it merges multiple equations and proof conclusions into coarse items and omits many independently inventoryable paper claims; additionally, the authored Delta>=1 infinite-rank item had no standalone row in the frozen fresh inventory.
reproduction_steps: Compare the 89 frozen protocol.phase1_inventory rows against contracts/numerical_scope_claims.json.
Accept only exact one-to-one canonical mappings; do not collapse multiple Eq. (7), Eq. (9), Eq. (10), isotropic-amplitude, asymptotic, or phase-regime rows into one authored item.
Observe that contracts/numerical_scope_claims.json contains the standalone Delta>=1 infinite-transfer-rank item but the frozen inventory has no exact standalone counterpart.

findings.claim: The scientific and runner tests pass, but the render-contract test cannot run in-place from the sanitized bundle because it looks for implementation/outputs/data while the frozen files are packaged under generated_data/outputs/data.
reproduction_steps: From implementation/, run PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest -q tests.
Observe 47 passed tests and one FileNotFoundError in test_render_contract_preserves_frozen_scientific_data.
Compare the path expected by implementation/tests/test_render_figures.py with the packaged generated_data/outputs/data paths.
